memories.text: There's something I'm avoiding in stillness. The fog, the crash, the rent stress — these aren't just inconveniences I'm managing around. They're things I'm afraid to sit with, and momentum feels safer than facing them directly.

I run from the crash rather than accepting it. The "bright feeling" becomes something I chase and protect, even as the evidence of depletion mounts entry by entry. By the time I finally listen, I'm completely bottomed out — which suggests I only stop when I have no choice.

I have a strong pattern of mistaking emotional highs for physical readiness — when I feel bright and hopeful, I override what my body is actually telling me, and I keep finding new justifications to keep moving rather than stopping. The rationalizations shift (eat, don't eat, exercise, connection, food again) but the underlying avoidance stays the same.

I got to the park and I made it to my friend's, which matters — but I kept circling back to movement and skipping meals, the same old pattern of burning instead of feeding, and I suspect I didn't land as softly at night as I promised myself I would.

The rent stress is real and present, but I keep naming it only to set it aside — "exercise will help me think about it." I'm using momentum as an escape from the thing that actually needs my attention.

I'm someone who experiences genuine highs and leans hard into them, almost desperately, as if I know the crash is coming and I'm trying to outrun it. "This bright feeling won't last forever" keeps appearing — and I wonder if I'm chasing the feeling more than I'm actually living my life.
